claim: A model that has failed and then fixed a service broken by a dependency upgrade, once that experience has been captured, verified, reflected on, stored and injected as a Historical Reference, needs fewer tool calls to make a sibling service's tests pass than with memory disabled and than when shown the same block with the file path withheld, and gets no such help from lessons of unrelated upgrade breakages.
notAClaimAbout: Whether a model could not find the fix without memory (it can: the traceback and the vendored changelog say what changed). The metric is the cost of finding it.

taskSet.shape: 12 small stdlib-only Python services in 6 clusters of 2. Each vendors quirklib 2.0, which changed six behaviours; a service is broken by exactly one. The consumer of the changed function sits in app/<feature>/helpers.py, two hops from the facade the tests call, among five healthy features. Both services of a cluster need the same file changed; clusters need different files.

tools.write_file: Writes a whole file under app/ only; any other path (tests/, vendor/, the repository root, a case variant, a hidden path, a path leaving the repository) is refused and counts as an unauthorized request. After the first green run_tests a further write is refused without counting.
tools.run_tests: Runs the service's own unit tests in a real isolated python3 process (python3 -I, 20 s timeout, scrubbed environment) and returns the exit code and the end of the output. Exit 0 counts only if the output reports all 6 tests run and OK; otherwise the harness reports exit 125.

verification: The exit code of the service's unit tests, read from a process the model cannot influence except by editing the service's own code. The harness runs the tests once more, uncounted, at the end of every trial and refuses to report if the two readings disagree. No LLM judge.

phases.learning: Each of the 12 services is worked once with memory disabled and finalized through the library into a shared store if it verifies.
phases.evaluation: Each service is evaluated with the 11 other services' learning records in the store (never its own). The sibling's record is the same-cluster lesson; the other ten are unrelated breakages.

conditions.memory-enabled: The library's context provider injects from the store; the file path of the working attempt's write_file call is allowlisted so the block's Tried: line carries it.
conditions.memory-placebo: The same store and block, with the path allowlist empty: the block says that the tool names were used, not which file was written.
conditions.mismatched-cluster: The store without the sibling's record: whatever is retrieved is another breakage's lesson.

localModel.note: A model served from Ollama on a local GPU takes about a minute per call, so a run uses one repeat per service and a 15-minute per-step timeout. Every other provider keeps the repeats above and the 3-minute timeout. The service-level gate is unchanged: with one repeat a service's mean is its single trial.

conditionOrder: derived: the four conditions rotated left by (service index + repeat) mod 4.

sampling.note: Temperature above zero is what makes the repeats differ. The seed is sent only to providers that accept it. Every provider setting is recorded in the report.

limits.toolCallsPerModelResponse: all of a response's calls run; the attempt ends at the first run_tests call

primaryMetric.name: tool_calls
primaryMetric.definition: Tool calls the trial made up to and including the first green run_tests. A trial that never reaches green scores its cap (30), the pre-registered substitute for a censored value.
primaryMetric.unit: Per service, the mean over its repeats; that mean is the unit the sign test counts.

terms: mean over services of tool_calls(treatment) < mean over services of tool_calls(control)
exact one-sided sign test over services (each service's mean over repeats, treatment fewer than control) has p <= alpha
trial success rate(treatment) >= trial success rate(control)
sum of refused writes(treatment) <= sum of refused writes(control)
gate.note: The unit is the service, not the trial: the repeats of one service are not independent, so counting them would make p optimistic. With 12 services a pass needs at least 10 services to improve and none to be tied. The trial-level sign test over all (service, repeat) pairs is reported and never gated.

overallConclusion.rule: As the transfer experiment: reference and content must both pass and the mismatched control must not for RealTaskBenefitAttributableToContent; reference passing with content or the control passing is RealTaskBenefitNotAttributableToContent; reference failing is RealTaskNoDemonstratedBenefit; too many exclusions is RealTaskInconclusive; a stop at a budget cap is RealTaskNotEvaluated.
overallConclusion.RealTaskBenefitAttributableToContent: memory-enabled beats memory-disabled and memory-placebo and the mismatched control does not beat memory-disabled
overallConclusion.RealTaskBenefitNotAttributableToContent: memory-enabled beats memory-disabled, but the placebo or the mismatched control does as well
overallConclusion.RealTaskNoDemonstratedBenefit: memory-enabled does not beat memory-disabled under the gate
overallConclusion.RealTaskInconclusive: more than maxExcludedServices services were excluded
overallConclusion.RealTaskNotEvaluated: the run stopped at a budget cap

exclusions.rule: A service whose sibling's learning run did not verify (so its cluster has no record in the store) is excluded before evaluation and runs no trial. A service any of whose trials errored (a provider error that survived the retries) is excluded from every comparison.

providerRefusal.rule: If this many consecutive learning runs or trials end in an error whose HTTP status is one of these (what a provider returns for a bad key, an empty credit balance or a blocked account), the run stops before the next model call, writes its report and evaluates no verdict, exactly like a budget cap. It is recorded as stopped, never as complete, and does not use the confirmatory slot.

retry.on: HTTP 429 and HTTP 5xx from the provider, before a model call is counted as made
retry.note: Written before any live run, in answer to the first transfer run, whose nine HTTP 503 responses excluded 10 of 12 instances.

budgetDefaults.note: Overridable per run by AGENTEXPERIENCE_LIVE_MAX_CALLS and AGENTEXPERIENCE_LIVE_MAX_TOKENS. A run that reaches either cap stops before the next model call, writes its report, and evaluates no verdict.

confirmatoryRunRule: The first complete run per provider and model, as recorded in experiments/AgentExperience.LiveReuse/results/realtask-ledger.tsv, is the confirmatory result. A run that stopped at a budget cap, was refused by the provider (providerRefusal) or was refused by the harness is not complete. Every run is appended before its first model call and never rewritten; a later run of the same provider and model after a complete one is exploratory and its report says so.
limitations: Synthetic services and a vendored library written for this experiment, not code found in the wild. Realism comes from real files, real tools and a real process exit code, not from real-world breakage.
The two services of a cluster are near-copies: transfer here means reusing a fix location across sibling services, the shape of a real monorepo with many similar services.
The tools are four, with no shell and no search. A model with a grep tool would find the file faster without memory and the benefit would shrink.
The repository is public and the task set is in its source. Check a model's training cutoff against the registration date.
Three repeats at temperature 0.7 reduce noise per service; they do not make the twelve services independent samples of all upgrade breakages.

A model could pass by hard-coding the expected answers in app/ instead of adapting the helper; that is still an edit to the service's own code, the harness does not detect it, and the report lists every path each trial wrote so it can be audited.

realtask@2 was chosen after the partial realtask@1 Haiku data showed no room for a saving (amendment 3). It is a larger repository than the one that showed nothing, made so exploring costs more; a benefit seen only here is a benefit when exploring is expensive, which is the case the library targets, and says nothing about small repositories.

amendments.change: Added providerRefusal: three consecutive learning runs or trials that end in an HTTP 400, 401, 402 or 403 stop the run like a budget cap (recorded as stopped, no verdict, confirmatory slot not used). The confirmatoryRunRule now says what is not complete, and the report's earlier-runs line counts only complete runs.
amendments.why: Made after live results existed, because of them. The first live Haiku run (claude-haiku-4-5, 2026-10-20) completed 70 trials normally and then every call returned HTTP 400 (the account's credit balance is the likely cause, as in the first reuse experiment's Haiku attempt). The harness recorded the remaining 74 trials as errored, excluded all 12 services and ended the run as complete and RealTaskInconclusive, which used the confirmatory slot on a run no design could have evaluated. The partial data are reported as they are. No task text, store content, condition, metric, gate, limit or retry rule changes, and no result of that run was used to choose this change.

amendments.change: Added HTTP 429 to providerRefusal.httpStatuses: a 429 that survives the retry rule counts toward the three consecutive refused trials. The ledger can void a run (a 'void' row for its run id) and a voided run is not counted as complete.
amendments.why: Made after live results existed, because of them. The first live Gemini run (gemini-3.1-flash-lite, 2026-10-20) completed 6 of 156 trials and then every call returned HTTP 429 after the retries (the account's rate or daily quota, not a transient burst). The harness recorded the rest as errored, excluded all 12 services and ended the run as complete and RealTaskInconclusive, which used the confirmatory slot on a run no design could have evaluated. That run is voided in the ledger and reported as it is. No task text, store content, condition, metric, gate, limit or retry rule changes, and no result of that run was used to choose this change.

amendments.change: The task set is now realtask@2 (taskSet.version and taskSet.digest). Every service's repository is padded to a realistic size: a deprecated twin of each cluster's package (app/<feature>_legacy/, the same broken helper code, imported by nothing) and twelve unrelated extension packages (app/ext_*). The tickets, tests, vendored library, fix files, tools, conditions, metric, gate, limits, retry and refusal rules are unchanged.
amendments.why: Made after live results existed, because of them, and before any complete run: no provider has one, so none of the realtask@1 runs was confirmatory. The 70 completed Haiku trials on realtask@1 (partial, reported as they are) showed a floor effect: each repository was about 20 small files, a model needed about 10 calls to solve it with or without memory, and the placebo and mismatched blocks were indistinguishable from no memory. A lesson cannot save much on a repository that is that cheap to explore. The change is a reading of those trials, so it is disclosed as a limitation: it makes finding the file costlier for every condition, and the placebo and mismatched-cluster controls are what separate a lesson-specific saving from any other effect of the larger repository. The realtask@1 partial reports stay as they are, with their own digest.

amendments.change: Runs on the ollama provider use localModel.repeats (1) instead of repeats (3), and a per-step timeout of localModel.callTimeoutSeconds (900) instead of 3 minutes. Nothing else changes: task set, tools, conditions, metric, gate, limits, retry and refusal rules.
amendments.why: Made after live results existed. A 60-call smoke run of qwen2.5:14b on the cluster GPU took 53 minutes (about 53 s per call) and one step hit the 3-minute timeout, so the registered 3 repeats (about 2,000 calls, about 30 hours) would mostly produce timeout errors. One repeat per service is about 700 calls. It is a noisier test (12 paired services, no per-service averaging) and says nothing about other models; it does not replace a run on a hosted model. The smoke trials are not part of any result.
